visitor.headline: Every voice counts once, and reads at once.
visitor.standfirst: VoteLive is a newsroom for your questions: you ask them, the community votes, and the results go to print live.
visitor.p1: A poll starts with a well-asked question. On VoteLive you write it yourself, or hand a topic to the AI, which suggests neutral wording and coherent answers. You proofread, correct, then publish.
visitor.p2: Once the poll is open, each participant casts a single ballot. The figures update instantly on the screen of everyone following the poll. Among friends or colleagues, a group chat can settle things too: “Where do we go this weekend?”
visitor.step1: A question, two to ten answers, a closing time. Or just a topic, and the AI suggests a first draft.
visitor.step2: For everyone, for a few guests, or for a group. You decide whether results are read live or at closing.
visitor.step3: Every ballot cast updates the figures on every reader’s screen, without reloading the page.
visitor.step4: At the set time, the poll closes by itself and participants are told the final results.
visitor.rubric1: One account, one vote. The rule is checked by the server and guaranteed by the database, even when two clicks go out at the same time.
visitor.rubric2: Private messages and group chats in real time, with read receipts. A group can run its own polls.
visitor.rubric3: The AI suggests a neutral question and clear answers. Nothing is published without your review.

newPoll.title: Write a poll
newPoll.subtitle: Write the question yourself, or order a first proof from the AI and then correct it.
newPoll.guide1: Avoid double questions: an “and” in a question often hides two polls.
newPoll.guide2: The question must not suggest an answer. Prefer “What do you think of…” to “Don’t you agree that…”.
newPoll.guide3: Every reader should recognise themselves in a single answer.
newPoll.guide4: Give readers time to vote: a few hours for a hot topic, a few days otherwise.
